body.statement: Exhibit explicit evaluable functions \(r(n,T,c)\) and \(\ell(n,T,c)\), a total finite-data estimator \(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\), and a total connected interval \(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\) such that, for universal \(0<a_0\leq A_0<\infty\) and every \(n,T\geq1\), \(c\in[0,1]\), \(a_0r(n,T,c)\leq R(n,T,c)\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_T}E_{P^n}[(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}-\psi_T(P,c))^2]\leq A_0r(n,T,c)\) and \(a_0\ell(n,T,c)\leq L(n,T,c)\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_T}E_{P^n}[\operatorname{length}(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c})]\leq A_0\ell(n,T,c)\). Require \(I^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,T,c}\in\mathcal C_{n,T,c}\), state finite computational cost, include every logarithmic transition and saturation factor, and derive from these functions necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform consistency along every \(T=T_n,c=c_n\) and necessary and sufficient conditions for \(R/R^{\mathrm{or}}\) or \(L/L^{\mathrm{or}}\) to diverge in order.
body.justification: This question is the theorem-level kernel: one matched all-sample phase diagram jointly governs estimation, honest inference, consistency, and the value of propensity knowledge.
body.gap: No inspected result, including KimKennedyNaimi2021, KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies, MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022, or ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete, gives an unrestricted nested-prefix frontier for a propensity-dependent target.
body.consumer: The EAGeR-style long-history workflow and the \(\texttt{imtp}\) implementation obtain a theorem stating when sample size must grow with history complexity despite bounded oracle weights.

obligation.what_is_open: The full matched functions \(r(n,T,c)\) and \(\ell(n,T,c)\), including every intermediate logarithmic transition, together with an attaining interval and all-sequence consistency and oracle-penalty characterizations.
obligation.obstruction: This target depends on the unresolved compatible-prefix approximation/testing dual. The endpoint estimator and paired-prior converse match only at zero shift and beyond the birthday-collision depth; the proved finite-depth optimization is an honest bracket, not an exact phase diagram.
obligation.attempted: Combined the natural-mean procedure, empirical truncated-tree plug-ins, the dimension-free influence bound, Bernoulli benchmarks, and complementary-context mixtures over every admissible prefix depth. No reduction to a static tilt is valid, and the resulting intermediate upper and lower optimizations remain separated.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved phase information is exact at two boundaries.  At \(c=0\), \(R(n,T,0)\asymp n^{-1}\) and \(L(n,T,0)\asymp n^{-1/2}\) for every \(T\).  If \(T\geq2\lceil\log_4(100n^2)\rceil\), then
\[
 R(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\},
 \quad
 L(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}.
\]
In this long-history regime, uniform consistency along \(n\to\infty\) is equivalent to \(c_n\to0\), and the unknown- and known-propensity orders agree exactly when \(c_n=O(n^{-1/2})\); the risk and length ratios have orders \(1+nc_n^2\) and \(1+\sqrt n c_n\), respectively.  Outside that regime, the explicit finite optimization and paired lower envelope recorded for \(\mathrm{oeq:compatible\text{-}prefix\text{-}approximation}\) are valid total finite-sample bounds.  They recover saturation and shrinking strength, but they do not determine all intermediate logarithmic transitions or furnish necessary and sufficient consistency and oracle-penalty conditions for arbitrary \((T_n,c_n)\).
